captions.instagram:
How does colour grading work?

Film a street, three faces and a sunset in 3D, then grade them yourself. A real grading pipeline runs on your graphics card: log footage through a 3D LUT, lift, gamma and gain wheels you can drag, live waveform, parade and vectorscope, a tracked power window, teal and orange, and HDR in nits.

→ Cinema cameras record log: a flat, grey picture that keeps every stop of light.
→ A 3D LUT moves every colour to its place, and the flat file becomes a Rec.709 picture.
→ Lift moves the blacks, gamma the middle, gain the whites: the waveform follows every turn.
→ Three very different skin tones, one line on the vectorscope: the skin-tone line.
→ Two cameras, two times of day: balance the grey chart, match exposure, and the cut disappears.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/gradeclear (link in bio)

Box No. 066 of 365. Follow @glassbox.how for a new "how it works" every day.

youtubeLong.title: How does colour grading work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Film a street, three faces and a sunset in 3D, then grade them yourself. A real grading pipeline runs on your graphics card: log footage through a 3D LUT, lift, gamma and gain wheels you can drag, live waveform, parade and vectorscope, a tracked power window, teal and orange, and HDR in nits.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/gradeclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/gradeclear

In this video:
• Log keeps the light, a LUT makes it watchable. Cinema cameras record log: a flat, grey file that keeps about 7.8 stops above a grey card, where a Rec.709 video file clips just 2.5 stops up.
• Lift, gamma, gain, checked on scopes. Three colour wheels move the shadows, mid-tones and highlights.
• Matching shots. Shots filmed hours apart, on different cameras, must cut together.
• Secondaries change only part of the picture. A qualifier selects a range of hue, saturation and brightness, like only the sky or one shirt.
• The look. Teal and orange works because the two are complementary and skin sits on the orange side.
• Delivery: nits and gamuts. SDR is graded for 100 nits of white, cinema screens about 48, and HDR TVs reach 1,000 or more, giving highlights far more room.
